Satie saves a darker chord for his second ending. Other returns arrive in a new key or with the whole orchestra behind them.
Bach fits four voices under a pianist’s hands. Handel lets a whole choir trade a tune, then brings everyone together on the same words.
Ravel changes the instrument and lets the tune stay put. Elsewhere, a whole orchestra becomes strings and harp, or a piano becomes a drowned cathedral.
A thunderous piano étude and a hushed operatic prelude fit into the same short break. Each recording is a complete piece or movement.
